Use case: historical-scene
Asset type: Matkakirja city-guide detail; a newly generated photorealistic historical illustration, not a documentary photograph.
Create exactly one landscape image, native 1536 x 1024 pixels, 3:2, opaque sRGB RGB PNG. Entirely new generation from this text, no source image pixels.
Subject and era: The ruined OLD Victorian House of Commons debating chamber, London, in May 1941 just after the bombing and fire of the night of 10–11 May. A quiet hollow roofless shell, viewed from inside the chamber along its long axis. This is Barry and Pugin's compact oblong debating room before the 1950 rebuilding, with intimate parliamentary proportions and opposing bench areas. It is a rectangular chamber of moderate height and length, not a vast church nave. The side wall sections have repeated pairs of narrow pointed Perpendicular Gothic windows with tracery, many panes shattered; these are the narrow windows of the old chamber rather than the broad postwar arches. Pale limestone masonry is stained with smoke and soot. Remnants of elaborately carved dark oak wall panelling and fragments of the perimeter viewing-gallery structure are badly burned. The opposing rows of wooden benches have collapsed into low heaps to left and right. The central aisle is partly visible through the debris, leading towards the battered far end. Charred timber ceiling members and roof beams lie broken across debris, with a little twisted structural ironwork. The former pitched timber-panelled ceiling and roof are gone, so a pale grey daylight sky is plainly visible above the surviving walls. A few small glass fragments among ash and stone dust, with modest lingering smoke haze.
Composition: A human eye-level camera inside the room, looking along the long axis slightly off-centre. Wide but believable 35 mm documentary lens perspective, show both side sections and the open roof, broken timber and collapsed benches in foreground and middle distance. Keep the chamber recognisably compact and oblong, with restrained neo-Gothic detailing. Use an original spatial arrangement, not a re-creation of any surviving artwork or source photograph.
Style and light: Camera-shot photorealistic appearance, soft overcast daylight after a smoky morning, muted stone grey and charred brown, realistic irregular scorch marks, splintered wood, ash, dust, gentle atmospheric softness. Quiet, sober non-graphic aftermath. No flames, cinematic devastation spectacle, HDR, extreme contrast, vivid orange firelight, watercolour or painted surface.
Constraints: No people, casualties, bodies, wounds, blood, flags, words, letters, numbers, signage, logos, brands, watermarks, border, loose printed papers, legible inscriptions, modern objects, electronics, present-day fixtures or clean surviving green benches. Do not depict the 1950 chamber destroyed again. No giant cathedral, nave, altar, intact rib-vaulted stone roof, fantasy ruin, or exaggerated ornamental church. Do not reproduce Pitchforth's watercolour or any painting, etching, photograph, or its composition. Create a new scene using historical textual architectural facts only. Do not put the AI disclosure or any text into the image.
